findings: chainSet is the finite set of labels actually visited by a walk. Append is set union, subwalk is set inclusion, and a covered junction saves at least one chain from the sum. The singleton-color internal splice adds no new label.
last_disallowed_edge extracts an actual incompatible edge followed by a suffix allowed under the ancestor-source filter. It does not claim that the suffix is optimal.

In incompatible_guard, incompatibility forces a cross-chain entrance to a covered chain, valid at b for source u but invalid at b for source s. The earlier entry z=first(s,b) is reachable from s and reaches b. If u reached z, first(u,z)=b and first_spec would give b reaches z; DAG antisymmetry would force z=b, contradicting incompatibility.

A true minimum s-to-z filtered walk, an actual monochromatic z-to-b splice, and the compatible suffix form a valid s-to-t walk. The shared covered junction gives distance(s,t)+1 <= distance(s,z)+count(q).
The dichotomy applies this to a true u-to-t minimizing walk. If that walk is already s-compatible, ordinary append yields the triangle alternative; otherwise the proved guard alternative follows.
